findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: The set built by this method is consumed by UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource, which pass it into `UserModel.GROUPS`; the user store interprets those values as *group* IDs. This method adds `groupResource.getId()` (the internal authorization Resource UUID) and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, which does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` — group resources are named by the group id (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup), so passing the resource id makes the lookup miss and fall back to the shared 'Groups' resource. On top of that, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` never calls `setType(...)` on the resources it creates, so `findByType(server, "Groups")` only ever returns the shared 'Groups' resource and never the per-group ones. Consequence: when an admin is granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the all-groups resource (and cannot view all users via roles/scope), the returned set is non-empty and contains a non-group UUID, so the user search/count is filtered by a group id that matches nothing and returns no users even though the admin should see members of every group; per-group grants are never turned into group ids at all. Add `groupResource.getName()` (the group id) and treat an all-groups grant as 'no filter' (empty set) or expand it to all group ids. The new tests only cover per-group grants and never list users/count with an all-groups member permission, which is why this is not caught.

findings.title: Global canManage() accepts the group VIEW scope, allowing group creation with read-only permission
findings.body: `canManage()` returns true when the caller only has an all-groups VIEW permission (`hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). This no-arg method is used for enforcement, not just UI: `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an admin who was granted only read access to all groups can create new top-level groups. The per-group counterpart `canManage(GroupModel)` (lines 74-80) correctly requires only the MANAGE scope, so this looks like a copy of `canView()`. Restrict the global check to `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`.

findings.title: Group removal fails when the V2 group permission management methods are reached
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides the management methods (`setPermissionsEnabled`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource`, ...) with UnsupportedOperationException, but they are still reachable. `AdminPermissions.registerListener()` registers a `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent` listener whenever the V1 feature is enabled, and its handler executes `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` (AdminPermissions.java line 94). `management()` returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 feature is enabled, and MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() now returns GroupPermissionsV2 (before this PR it returned the V1 implementation, where the call was a harmless no-op). So in a deployment with both features enabled, deleting any group throws UnsupportedOperationException inside the synchronous provider event and the deletion fails with a 500. The same unsupported methods are reached from `GroupResource.get/setManagementPermissions`, which are only guarded by the V1 feature check. The listener and endpoints must not dispatch to methods the selected implementation rejects (skip the V1 cleanup when V2 is active, or make GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled a no-op).

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never get the new Groups resource type and scopes
findings.body: `init()` returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client (lines 250-252), so the newly added 'Groups' resource and its scopes (`manage-members`, `view-members`, `manage-membership`) are only created for realms that enable admin permissions after this change. For a realm that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions (the V2 feature is a preview that existed before this PR), the client exists without them. Afterwards every group permission check goes through GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(), which falls back to `getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`; that returns null for such clients and the code immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` and `new ResourcePermission(null, resource.getScopes(), ...)`, producing an exception (500) for group listing/checks, while creating a group permission fails in `getOrCreateResource()` with ModelException("No scopes found.") because the group scopes were never created. `init()` needs to add missing resource types/scopes to an existing client (or a migration/versioning step is required), and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission should null-check the resource-type resource before dereferencing it.

findings.title: Permissions targeting a group are rendered with the raw group id
findings.body: `getResourceName()` resolves USERS resources to a friendly name ('All users' or the username) but has no branch for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE. Group resources are created with the group id as their name (`resolveGroup()` returns `group.getId()`), so the resources listed for a group scope permission in the admin API/console are group UUIDs instead of group names. Add a GROUPS branch analogous to the USERS one (resolve the name via `session.groups().getGroupById(...)`).

findings.title: Group listing now performs one permission evaluation per group
findings.body: The pre-computed `canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView()` short-circuit was removed here and in GroupResource.getSubGroups (line 179), so `canView(g)` is invoked for every returned group. For an admin who holds a global group VIEW/MANAGE permission but no realm-management role - exactly the case the FGAP v2 feature targets - GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel) does not short-circuit on the global grant: it performs a resource lookup plus a policy evaluation per group. Listing a realm with many groups therefore executes one authorization evaluation per group instead of one for the whole request, on every group/subgroup listing call.

findings.title: Javadoc documents a Stream return value for a Set-returning method
findings.body: The `@return` tag says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns `Set<String>`. Callers reading the contract will assume wrong semantics (stream vs. materialized set, and the Javadoc's 'Stream of IDs' wording). Correct the documented return type.
